clue.text: Upright character starts to nod cynically about old language

parts.note: the letter I is drawn as a single upright stroke

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: first letters of nod and cynically, N and C
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A description of someone giving a sceptical nod while talking about some ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inca is used for Quechua, the tongue spoken by the people of the Inca empire in Peru.

clue.text: Rare businessman spurning transactions containing fossil bits

indicators.note: spurning says the abbreviation for transactions is rejected from the word

parts.note: industrial is a rare noun for someone engaged in industry
TR is a dictionary abbreviation for transactions

explanation.surface: An uncommon tycoon refuses to do deals involving pieces of fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: Indusial limestone is a freshwater rock full of the fossilised cases of caddis-fly larvae.

clue.text: Detective thus turned up carrying boxes

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Det is the short form of detective used in police ranks, as in Det Sgt
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A detective arrives with some boxes in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cist is a stone burial chest, so a cisted grave contains such coffin-like boxes.

clue.text: Honour surrounding prize for each person

indicators.note: surrounding says the honour word goes around the prize word

parts.note: an ace is an honour card in bridge
pie is something prized, as in pie in the sky

explanation.surface: An award is given to each person in the honours list.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning to or for each one individually.

clue.text: With Jags aplenty goof admitted to being stuffed?

indicators.note: admitted to says the word for goof is let into the word for being stuffed

parts.note: sated means full up, stuffed with food
to err is to goof, make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone owning lots of Jaguar cars makes a blunder after a heavy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Jags are not cars here but jags, sharp projections. 'admitted to' lets ERR into SATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated edge has a row of sharp teeth or notches, so it is covered in jags.

clue.text: Positions of responsibility from new Persian hosts

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into something fresh, a different order

explanation.surface: Important jobs come from fresh Persian landlords.
explanation.definitionFit: Senatorships are the offices held by senators, posts carrying public duty.

clue.text: Admit couple mostly needling old uncle

indicators.note: needling means piercing into, so the trimmed couple goes inside the old uncle

parts.note: eme is an old word for an uncle

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter of the word for couple

parts.note: a brace is a pair or couple

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the pair has been mostly irritating an old relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Eme is an old Scots and dialect word for an uncle, rarely seen outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or a person is to accept or receive them, which is a sense of admit.

clue.text: Exuberant Cuban's tour I'm starting

indicators.note: starting is used as startled, jumping, so the letters leap into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively speaker announces they are beginning a tour of Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambunctious means boisterous and full of uncontrolled high spirits.

clue.text: Absolute fool trimmed pasta

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for absolute, as in the absolute temperature scale

indicators.note: trimmed means the last letter of the word for fool is cut off

parts.note: a nellie is a silly or soft person

explanation.surface: A complete idiot cut the pasta short.
explanation.definitionFit: Anelli are small ring-shaped pieces of pasta, the name being Italian for rings.

clue.text: Fern? A miserable specimen from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A girl called Fern is dismissed as a poor sort from down south.
explanation.definitionFit: Tara is the New Zealand name for bracken, a common fern.

clue.text: One right to leave Spenser's gloom for Scots to bear

indicators.note: to leave says one letter departs from the old word

parts.note: dreer is a form of drere, Spenser's word for gloom or dreariness
one R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A person's right to escape Spenser's melancholy, which Scots must put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Dree is Scots for to endure or suffer, as in dree one's weird.

clue.text: Main award for bravery initially awarded in the afternoon

parts.note: a water main is a pipe
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for gallantry

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is A

explanation.surface: A sailor's main bravery medal is presented one afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: PIP EMMA is old military signallers' phonetic speech for the letters PM; 'initially' takes just the first letter of awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Signallers spelt out PM as pip emma, so the phrase means post meridiem, after noon.

clue.text: Sort out a soul's broken pottery

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: ka is the soul or spiritual double in ancient Egyptian belief

explanation.surface: Sorting out a person's smashed crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostraka are potsherds, fragments of pottery used in ancient Greece for writing on.

clue.text: Pukka Asian channel getting divided and replaced

indicators.note: the word is cut into two halves and the halves swap places

parts.note: side is colloquial for a television channel, as in 'the other side'

explanation.surface: An authentic South Asian TV channel is split up and taken off air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting divided and replaced' splits SIDE as SI and DE and swaps the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Desi describes people or things authentically of the Indian subcontinent, local and genuine, which is what pukka means.

clue.text: Seem upset about core of clergy rising to the upper stratum?

indicators.note: about says the anagrammed letters go around the core of clergy
upset tells us the letters of seem are knocked into a new order
core of takes the central letters of the next word

parts.note: its middle two letters are E and R

explanation.surface: A churchman's ambition to climb into the upper class seems upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of' takes the central pair of a six-letter word. Emerse is a rare botanical word, so the question mark flags a fanciful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerse is a botanical term for parts of a water plant standing up above the surface, rising into the top layer.

clue.text: What we hope to do to weeds is completely rash, as it was

definitions.text: What we hope to do to weeds

parts.note: up means completely, as in eat up or burn up
rash is an obsolete verb meaning to tear or pull violently

explanation.surface: A gardener hopes the weeds will be dealt with in a hasty sweep, as was once done.
explanation.walkthrough: Rash looks like an adjective; it is an old verb for tearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To uptear is to pull out by the roots, the gardener's wish for weeds.

clue.text: Outside broadcast delayed a dedicated soul

parts.note: something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A religious person's televised event from a remote location runs behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a layperson who has offered themselves to a monastery and its religious life.

clue.text: Pure class act reproduced big shows

indicators.note: reproduced means the letters are made again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A genuine top-class performance is revived as major productions.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectaculars are lavish, large-scale entertainments or extravaganzas.

clue.text: Sets that decorate parish stable top to bottom

parts.note: par is the short form of parish used in church registers and on old maps

indicators.note: in a down clue, top to bottom moves the first letter to the end

parts.note: sure means stable, secure

explanation.surface: Decorations for the parish stable are put up from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Parures are matching sets of jewels or ornaments worn together.

clue.text: Distinguished secretary felt great compassion for Spenser

parts.note: SEC is the abbreviation for secretary
erned is a Spenserian form of yearned, felt deep pity

explanation.surface: A famous secretary was deeply moved by the poet Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: To secern is to discriminate or separate, so secerned means told apart.

clue.text: American's behind slightly novel idea for family of foxes, say

parts.note: can is American slang for the buttocks

indicators.note: slightly novel says the letters of idea are given a somewhat new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh idea about foxes comes from an American's rear end.
explanation.definitionFit: Canidae is the zoological family containing dogs, wolves and foxes.

clue.text: A passé composition about American who goes about skyclad

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go around the American abbreviation

parts.note: dite is an obsolete word for a composition or ditty

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned poem about an American who wanders around naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Skyclad, a pagan term, means naked; 'passé' marks dite as an obsolete word, and 'about' wraps the first pieces round the American.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adamite is a nudist, named after an early sect who imitated Adam's nakedness.

clue.text: 11th Cavalry Regiment's reinforced again in stiff hour out

indicators.note: in places the word for again inside what remains of stiff
out says the hour abbreviation is dropped from the word for stiff

parts.note: hard means stiff, rigid
more means again, as in 'once more'

explanation.surface: A US regiment's strengthened again during a gruelling hour's sortie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies letters; 'out' and 'in' do the work. The US 11th Armored Cavalry Regiment uses the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Armored, the American spelling, means protected with armour plating, so strengthened for battle.

clue.text: River and lake with small blackbirds in quaint way

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A river and a lake with little blackbirds in a charming way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousel is the old spelling of ouzel, a former name for the blackbird.

clue.text: One swears about published projection

indicators.note: about says the projection word goes round the published word

parts.note: a jut is a projecting part
a newspaper ran a story when it published it

explanation.surface: Someone curses about a ledge that has been made public.
explanation.definitionFit: A jurant is one who takes an oath, from Latin jurare, to swear.

clue.text: Well, in France not quite finished packing clear turnover

indicators.note: packing means the trimmed French word holds the clear word inside
not quite finished drops the last letter

parts.note: bien is French for well
to rid is to clear

explanation.surface: A French cook is almost done packing a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridie is a Scottish meat pasty, so the surface's 'turnover' is the pastry, not a business's sales.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a pastry folded over a filling, which is what a bridie is.

clue.text: Nationalist in running as usual with true freak

indicators.note: in says the nationalist's letter sits inside the rearranged letters
running means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nationalist candidate standing for election as usual is a genuine oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusus naturae is Latin for a sport of nature, a monster or abnormal creature.

clue.text: Naff trick turned short

indicators.note: turned means the word for trick is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: art means cunning, a trick or wile
shy means short, as in shy of the target

explanation.surface: A cheap trick backfired and fell short.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tasteless or cheap, which is exactly what trashy means.

clue.text: Criminal about to leg it caught easily

indicators.note: easily means the remaining letters are loosely rearranged
to leg it means to run off, so the about abbreviation leaves the word

parts.note: CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A crook about to run away is easily arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leg it' takes CA out of CAUGHT to leave UGHT, which 'easily' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent ruffian or criminal.

clue.text: Some war correspondents bow

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some journalists at the front take a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco is a musical direction to play with the bow rather than plucking.

clue.text: I'm spinning extra clause without depth — it's more muddy

indicators.note: spinning means I'm is turned round and read backwards
without says the depth abbreviation leaves the word for extra clause

parts.note: a rider is an additional clause added to a document

explanation.surface: A lawyer whirls around an extra clause that lacks depth, making things murkier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' turns I'M into MI, and 'without' takes D from RIDER to give RIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Miry means boggy or covered in mire, so its comparative describes something dirtier with mud.

clue.text: Male means to govern hoc loco

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein

explanation.surface: A man finds the way to rule in a particular place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoc loco is Latin for 'in this place', which herein also means.

clue.text: Port is a hotbed of debauchery

parts.note: a den is a haunt of vice, as in a den of iniquity

explanation.surface: A harbour town is described as a sink of vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Tightly tie up an ornamental plant

indicators.note: tightly here means drunkenly, tight being slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction to bind a decorative plant firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tightly looks like an adverb on tie up; read it as 'when tight', drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a garden flower grown for its showy trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Mags in ruin — that's to say taken in by what borders on gross

indicators.note: taken in by puts the following letters inside the edge letters
what borders on picks the outside letters of the next word

parts.note: its outer letters are G and S
loss means ruin, as in financial ruin
IE, id est, means that is to say

explanation.surface: Magazines going under, which is to say succumbing to vulgarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossies are magazines printed on shiny paper, and mags is the colloquial short word for magazines.

clue.text: Incline snare backwards close to ground

indicators.note: backwards means the word for snare is read in reverse

parts.note: a net is a snare for catching things

indicators.note: close to takes the final letter of the next word

parts.note: its final letter is D

explanation.surface: A trapper sets a snare low, near the ground, on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to have a tendency or lean towards something.
